content: The provided text appears to be a list of references from various studies, articles, and reports, primarily related to pharmaceutical policies, drug pricing, and healthcare systems. However, the majority of these entries are marked as Ineligible Study Design, indicating that they do not meet certain criteria for inclusion in a specific analysis or review. 1. Hughes DA explored the concept of value-based pricing in pharmaceuticals, questioning whether it serves as an incentive for innovation or results in zero net benefit. This study was published in Pharmacoeconomics in 2011. 2. Ikegami N and Campbell JC analyzed Japan's healthcare system, focusing on cost containment and reform efforts. Their findings were published in Health Affairs in 2004. 3. Imbaud D, Morin A, Picard S, and Toujas F conducted an evaluation of France's generic drug policy, detailed in a report published in 2012. 4. Inotai A and Kalo Z examined risk-sharing methods in middle-income countries, with their findings published in Acta Pharmaceutica Hungarica in 2012. 5. Iskrov G and Stefanov R discussed the prospects of risk-sharing agreements for innovative therapies in Bulgaria, particularly in the context of deficit spending. Their work appeared in Frontiers in Public Health in 2015. 6. Jaeger K reported on the $734 billion in healthcare savings attributed to generic drugs in the United States, as published in Pharma Times in 2009. 7. Jiang ST, Yin XZ, Wang WH, and Liu YP investigated the relationship between price regulation and the sales volume of 146 types of medicines, with their study published in Pharma Care Research in 2004. 8. Jin C, Chen Z, and He L studied the zero-profit drug supply policy and its associated reimbursement mechanisms in Shanghai's medical institutions. Their findings were published in the Chinese Journal of Health Policy in 2010. 9. Jing C, Xizi Z, Liang Z, and Shi LW analyzed drug price regulation experiences in Germany, Japan, and Taiwan, providing insights for China's pharmaceutical policies. This study was published in China Pharmacy in 2017. 10. Jones GH, Carrier MA, Silver RT, and Kantarjian H examined strategies that delay or prevent the availability of affordable generic drugs in the United States. Their findings were published in Blood in 2016. 11. Jun G reviewed the effects of reference pricing and other pharmaceutical pricing policies on healthcare systems, as published in the Chinese Journal of Evidence-Based Medicine in 2008. 12. Kaiser U and Méndez SJ investigated how drug prices respond to a shift from external to internal reference pricing, using evidence from a Danish regulatory reform. Their findings were published in a ZEW Discussion Paper in 2015. 13. Kajdiž R and Bojnec Š analyzed the impact of price regulation and reimbursement policies on public expenditures for medicinal products, with their study published in Zdrav Vestn in 2012. 14. Kaltenboeck A and Bach PB discussed variations in value-based pricing for drugs, as published in JAMA in 2018. 15. Kanavos P, Ferrario A, Nicod E, and Sandberg D evaluated tender systems for outpatient pharmaceuticals in the European Union, focusing on evidence from the Netherlands and Germany. This study was published by EMINET in 2012. 16. Kaplan WA, Ritz LS, Vitello M, and Wirtz VJ reviewed policies promoting the use of generic medicines in lowand middle-income countries, covering literature from 2000 to 2010. Their findings were published in Health Policy in 2012. 17. Kelley LT, Tenbensel T, and Johnson A compared pharmaceutical cost and coverage policies in Ontario and New Zealand, with their study published in Health Policy in 2018. 18. Kohler JC, Mitsakakis N, Saadat F, Byng D, and Martinez MG examined the role of pharmaceutical pricing transparency in Brazil's public procurement system. Their findings were published in Global Health in 2015. 19. Luo J, Sarpatwari A, and Kesselheim AS proposed regulatory solutions to address high generic drug costs, as published in Open Forum Infectious Diseases in 2015. 20. Madsen LB, Ustrup M, Fischer TK, Bygbjerg IC, and Konradsen F evaluated the impact of reduced rotavirus vaccine prices on access in high-need areas, with their findings published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2012. 21. Maiga D and Williams-Jones B assessed the impact of market regulation on the price of essential medicines in Mali's private sector, as published in Health Policy in 2010. 22. Mardetko N, Ćosić M, and Kos M analyzed the cost-saving potential of therapeutic reference pricing systems for proton pump inhibitors in Slovenia, with their findings published in International Journal of Clinical Pharmacy in 2017. 23. Miraldo M compared reference pricing and co-payment systems in the pharmaceutical industry, focusing on price, quality, and market coverage. This study was published by CHE in 2007. 24. Mohamed O and Kreling DH investigated the effects of pricing policy changes on retail medicine prices in Egypt, as published in Value in Health Regional Issues in 2016. 25. Moorkens E, Simoens S, Troein P, and Declercq P analyzed the influence of policy measures on market dynamics for biosimilar and originator etanercept in Sweden, with their findings published in BioDrugs in 2019. 26. Morgan SG and Persaud N critiqued a new generic pricing scheme in Canada, highlighting its potential to maintain high prices and risk shortages. Their findings were published in CMAJ in 2018. 27. Moyé-Holz D, van Dijk JP, Reijneveld SA, and Hogerzeil HV evaluated policy approaches to improve medicine availability and affordability in Mexico, as published in Global Health in 2017. 28. Nguyen A, Kaplan WA, Laing R, and Press W reviewed policy options for promoting generic medicine use in developing and transitional countries, with their findings published by the World Health Organization in 2008. 29. Parlar-Chun R and Malek J demonstrated how price transparency can reduce seizure management costs among pediatric residents, as published in Journal of Investigative Medicine in 2019. 30. Patel HK, Dwibedi N, and Sansgiry SS assessed the impact of generic drug discount programs on managed care organizations, with their findings published in American Journal of Pharmacy Benefits in 2011.
